FB_LS_Creation_Days: Day 1: God made Day and Night. God said it was good.
Day 2: God made Sky and Sea. God said it was good.
Day 3: God made Land, Plants and Trees. God said it was good.
Day 4: God made Sun, Moon and Stars. God said it was good.
Day 5: God made Fish and Birds. God said it was good.
Day 6: God made Animals and People. God said it was good.
Day 7: On the seventh day God rested and everything God had made was good.
FB_FN_Adam_Eve: God made Adam and Eve and they were all so happy. They were best friends who loved each other. The beautiful garden of Eden was their home.
God said to Adam, 'You must understand, do not eat the fruit of this one tree, or you will die! Please obey this important command!'
There was a snake in the garden full of lies, poison, and hate. He was jealous watching God and Adam and Eve celebrate. He wanted to ruin their friendship.
The crafty snake shimmied up to Eve and whispered in her ear, 'What did God actually say? Don't trust God, He told you a lie! Eat the fruit, you won't die!'
Eve took a bite and shared it with Adam. They were filled with shame and sorrow. They realised that they were naked and hid in the shadows.
Then God came to the garden and called out their names, 'Where are you, Adam? Where are you, Eve?' They wouldn't answer because of their shame.
They answered, 'Yes! We ate the fruit of that certain tree!' Adam blurted out, 'It was the fault of this woman you gave to me!'
God cursed the lying snake forever to be the lowliest of all the wildlife. 'The snake will crawl on its belly all the days of its life.'
God and Adam and Eve could no longer celebrate. As they did not trust God their lives would be very hard and they were barred from Eden.
But God made a promise to Adam and Eve. One day a special baby would be born who will defeat the snake once and for all.
FB_LS_Cain_Abel: After Adam and Eve ate the fruit which God said not to touch, God told Adam that people would now have to work hard for their food.
God sent Adam and Eve away from the garden of Eden. Some time later they had two boys, first Cain and then Abel.
Cain loved to grow vegetables, but it was hard work digging in the hot sun and weeding the garden.
He brought the first of all the vegetables from his garden, as a gift to God. 'I will show God what I can do,' he thought.
Abel looked after the sheep. He brought his best little lamb to give to God. 'Thank you God for everything you give to me,' he prayed.
God saw the love and thankfulness that was in Abel's heart and God was pleased with the gift Abel gave to Him.
But Cain thought he had done all the work himself. He forgot that everything comes from God. God wasn't happy with his attitude.
Cain got angry and jealous, because he thought God should like his gift best. He didn't have a thankful attitude to God.
FB_LS_Cain_Anger: Be glad when someone else has, or does, something better than you. God knows when we are angry and jealous, or hurt others.
Adam and Eve had two boys. Abel, the younger brother, loved his sheep. He took a lamb to give to God.
God saw how much Abel loved the lamb and that he had given the best he had as a present to God.
Cain, the older brother, knew that God had been pleased with his younger brother's gift of a lamb. It made him jealous of his brother.
'I work hard and God should be pleased with me,' he thought. 'I am the best. I will teach my brother a lesson.'
Cain was so angry that he hit his brother Abel very hard and he died. Cain thought no one would ever know.
But God sees and knows everything. 'Where is your brother?' God asked Cain. 'Am I supposed to know where my brother is?' Cain replied.
Because Cain had done such a bad thing God sent him away to live in another country. God doesn't want us to hurt each other.
FB_LS_Noah_Ark: This story is found in the very first book in the Bible – the book of Genesis.
God said to Noah, 'It is going to rain and rain. Build a big boat with rooms for a mother and father of every animal.' Noah did what God told him to do.
It was a very, very big boat. Noah's family helped him too. Then they painted it all over to stop the water coming in. We call it 'Noah's Ark.'
When Noah had finished, a father and mother of each animal went into Noah's Ark. What a noise! So many animals!
God shut the door and it began to rain. The water got deeper and deeper. But Noah, his family and the animals were safe and dry inside the Ark.
After 40 days and nights, the rain stopped. It took a long time for the water to go away. Noah sent a bird to see if there was dry land.
At last the day came when everyone could go outside again! Noah and his family thanked God for keeping them safe and dry.
God made a beautiful rainbow in the sky. They had never seen a rainbow before! God has promised never to make it rain that much again!
FB_LS_Tower_Babel: Nimrod the mighty hunter was Noah's great grandson and the leader of his family. He decided to build a great city called Babel, with a tower reaching as high as heaven.
He lay awake at night thinking about his tower. The problem was there were not enough stones nearby, and stones were uneven — the tower would fall over if built too high.
He had an idea! Instead of round stones, he would make flat bricks, drying them in a fire until hard and strong. Now he could build higher than anyone ever had!
Everyone worked together building the tower. The bricks were held together with tar and the tower grew higher and higher — the tallest tower on earth.
God saw Nimrod's pride and knew that people could now do anything they dreamed of without trusting God at all. God decided to do something about it.
God worked a miracle. People suddenly began to speak with new words in different languages. The workers couldn't understand each other and got annoyed.
After a while groups of families who spoke the same way left Babel together to find their own places to live. Different languages spread all over the world.
FB_RP_Abraham_Calling: Abraham was from a city called Ur and staying at a place called Haran.
The Lord said to Abraham, 'Leave your country and go to the land I will show you. I will bless you and make your descendants into a great nation.'
'You will become famous and a blessing to others.'
'I will bless anyone who blesses you, but I will put a curse on anyone who curses you.'
'Everyone on earth will be blessed because of you.'
Abraham was 75 years old when God told him to leave the city of Haran.
He obeyed and left with his wife Sarai...
...his nephew Lot, his servants and all the possessions he had gathered in Haran.
When they came to the land of Canaan, Abraham went as far as the sacred tree of Moreh, in a place called Shechem.
The Canaanites were still living in the land at the time.
But the Lord appeared to Abraham and promised, 'I will give this land to your family forever.'
Abraham then built an altar to God there.
Later, the Lord spoke to Abraham in a vision.
'Abraham, don't be afraid, I will protect you and reward you greatly.'
But Abraham answered, 'Lord, All Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for – except children.'
'And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.'
'You have not given me children and this servant of mine will inherit everything.'
The Lord replied, 'No he won't. You will have a son of your own and everything you have will be his.'
Then the Lord took Abraham outside and said, 'Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.'
Abraham believed the Lord and the Lord was pleased with him.

FB_RG_Lot: Abram (later called Abraham) and his nephew Lot had moved to Canaan. Both had large flocks, and arguments broke out between their herdsmen over pasture.
So Abram said to Lot, 'Let's not have any quarrelling between your herdsmen and mine, for we are close relatives. Let's go our own ways. You choose first.'
Lot saw that the plain of Jordan had plenty of water and good land, and pitched his tents near Sodom. Abram went the other way, to live near Hebron.
Sodom and the other cities Lot chose were full of people who were very wicked. God decided the time had come to put an end to their wrongdoing.
God sent two angels into Sodom, where they found Lot at the city gate. He invited them in, and they warned him: 'Hurry and get out — the Lord is about to destroy the city!'
When Lot hesitated, the angels grasped his hand and his family's hands and led them out. 'Flee for your lives! Don't look back!' they urged.
God sent a terrible judgement on the wicked cities of the plain. Lot and his daughters obeyed and fled, but Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
The Bible warns us that it is far better to obey God and be safe, than disobey Him and face the consequences.
FB_LS_Abram: A long time ago, God made a special promise to Abram. 'Look at all the stars. There are too many to count.'
'You will have a big family, with lots of children. There will be too many to count.'
'How could this happen,' thought Abram. 'I don't even have one child of my own.' But Abram believed God would do just as He had promised.
And God told Abram that his family would be servants in another country, for four hundred long years.
Then God would send them to live in their own country that He would give them. God gave Abram a new name, 'Abraham.'
Abraham waited and waited. Sarah, his wife, was very old when they had a baby boy! God had not forgotten His promise!
They remembered God's promise. The Bible tells us that God did everything He said he would do.
FB_LS_Abraham_Isaac: We read in the Bible that Abraham loved God with all his heart. When God asked Abraham to give Him the one thing he loved the most, Abraham obeyed and trusted God.
Abraham and his wife Sarah had waited a long time to have a son of their own. Abraham loved Isaac more than anything else in the world and thanked God for him.
One day God tested Abraham. 'Take Isaac, your son, and give him to me as a present,' God said. 'Take him to a mountain I will show you.'
Early the next morning Abraham put wood for a fire on his donkey and went to the mountain with Isaac. It would be hard to give Isaac to God.
Isaac helped get the wood for the fire. 'Where is the lamb to give to God?' he asked. Abraham said, 'God will give us a lamb.'
Abraham put the wood on the altar of stones. He put Isaac, his special boy, on top. God knew that Abraham loved Him more than anything.
God said, 'Stop, Abraham! God has seen that you love Him, even more than you love your only boy. You listened to God, even when it was hard.'
God told Abraham that He had provided a lamb for him to give instead of Isaac. Abraham looked around and saw a ram caught by its horns in a bush.
Abraham and Isaac never forgot to make loving God the most important thing to do. When you obey and trust God He will never let you down.
FB_LS_Jacob_Ladder: In the Bible God promised Jacob that He would give him the land he was sleeping on for his descendants — many millions of them, living all over the world.
Isaac prayed and blessed his son Jacob before he went away to find a wife from his mother's family in Haran. As the sun was setting, Jacob looked for somewhere to sleep.
He made himself a pillow from smooth stones he found nearby and lay down to sleep. That night Jacob had a special dream.
He saw God's angels going up and down a ladder, between earth and heaven. God said, 'I am the God of Abraham and Isaac. I will give you and your descendants this land.'
'They will live in every corner of the world and be a blessing, and I will always be with you.' Jacob piled up the stones he had used as a pillow to mark the place, Bethel.
When he got to his mother's country he lifted a heavy stone lid from a well and helped some shepherds. They told him that Rachel and Leah were his cousins.
Rachel took Jacob home to meet his Uncle Laban. 'Come and work for me,' said Laban. 'I will work for you if I can marry Rachel,' Jacob replied.
'You can keep any animals that are not pure white when they are born and have patches on them,' Laban said. Jacob soon had many animals of his own.
FB_LS_Jacob_Israel: Jacob was on his way to meet his twin brother Esau and came to a river. Worried that Esau would still be angry with him, he sent his family across but stayed to pray.
Jacob loved God and wanted God to bless him and keep his family safe from his angry brother Esau. 'God forgive me and bless me,' he prayed.
A man passed by and Jacob realised he was sent by God. He caught hold of the man before he could go. 'Give me God's blessing,' he cried out.
The man tried to get away, but Jacob wrestled with him all night, determined to get God's blessing. In the struggle, his hip went out of joint, but he held on.
As the sun rose, the man blessed Jacob saying, 'You didn't give up easily. You held on until you got a blessing from God. From now on you shall be called Israel.'
Jacob crossed over the river to join his family. 'I have seen God face to face,' he said. 'He blessed me and gave me a new name — Israel.'
Since that day the children of Israel never ate the sinew in a joint of meat, because the angel touched Jacob's thigh and caused him to always walk with a limp.
FB_LS_Joseph_Dreams: We read in the Bible that Joseph had a promise from God, but it took many long years until Joseph's dreams came true.
One night, when Joseph was asleep, he had a very real dream about his brothers. He couldn't wait to get up and tell them all about it.
'We were tying together bundles of grain,' he told them. 'My sheaf stood up straight, but all your sheaves bowed down to mine.'
His older brothers were jealous of Joseph and got very angry. 'Do you really think we are going to bow down and let you be the boss of us?' they said.
Then Joseph had another dream, which he told his brothers and his father. 'The sun and moon and eleven stars bowed down to me,' he said.
His father spoke sternly to Joseph. 'Would your own family bow down in front of you?' he said. But in his heart he wondered if the dreams were from God.
Joseph's brothers went off to feed their father's sheep near Shechem. A while later, Israel sent Joseph to see how they were and bring back news.
From far off, his brothers saw him coming. 'Here comes the dreamer,' they said. 'Now is our chance to teach him a lesson.' But God was with Joseph and had a plan.
FB_LS_Joseph_Coat: This story is found in the very first book in the Bible – the book of Genesis.
Joseph had ten big brothers and one little brother. He loved God and he loved his family.
His father loved Joseph very much. He gave him a special present — a new coat with lots of colours — and showed it to his brothers.
Joseph's brothers were grumpy and jealous. They wanted the colourful new coat. They told Joseph to go away and were unkind to him.
The big brothers went to look after the sheep. One day his dad told Joseph to find them. Joseph put his new coat on straight away, always obeying his father.
It was a long way to go. Joseph had to ask someone the way. When he saw them he called out and waved. But his brothers were still grumpy.
They were not kind and took his coat away. Then they put him down inside a big hole. Joseph was sad, but he remembered that God was always with him.
The brothers saw traders coming on camels, going to Egypt. The brothers took Joseph and sold him to them to be taken away as a servant.
Joseph prayed and asked God to help him. He knew that God is always with us and wants us to do what is good and right.
FB_LS_Joseph_Brothers: Joseph's brothers were not kind to him. They sold him to some traders who took him to Egypt.
In Egypt he was sold as a servant who would have to work hard for his master. Joseph knew that God was with him wherever he was.
Poor Joseph was then put in jail for something he did not do. In jail he was good and kind, and everyone knew that Joseph loved God.
One night King Pharaoh had a dream. No one could help him understand it. He sent for Joseph, who asked God to help him understand the dream.
God told Joseph, 'Tell King Pharaoh to store lots and lots of corn, because soon people in other countries won't have enough to feed their families.'
Soon Joseph's brothers had no corn left to eat. Their father sent them to buy corn from King Pharaoh — not knowing Joseph was still alive and now in charge of Egypt's food.
Joseph gave corn to his brothers and some to take home to his father. When they returned for more he told them he was their brother and forgave them.
Joseph loved God and he looked after his family. God wants us to be kind to everyone, even if they are not kind to us.
